newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares rise again as Brazilian clouds pass.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares rise again as Brazilian clouds pass.

text.p: Chilean blue chips recouped from Tuesday's sell-off and rose sharply in early trade on foreign buying, as concerns eased on the Brazilian currency, brokers said.
The blue-chip IPSA index rose 1.07 percent to 132.66 points, while the all-share IGPA was up 0.53 percent to 5747.22 points.
"The panic about Brazil has lifted, but this rise is mainly driven by Wall Street," said a broker.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 16 points to 7,992.66 points.
He and other brokers were unsure what trajectory the market would take for the rest of the day, saying it would depend partly on bourses elsewhere in Latin America with all eyes on Sao Paulo.
The Bovespa index in Brazil opened 4.04 percent better, but later moderated that gain to a 2.45 percent recovery. On Tuesday, the Sao Paulo Exchange took a hard 8.5 percent hit.
Gainers included several blue chips that took a beating in Tuesday's slide, including CTC, up 2.1 percent to 3380 pesos, and Endesa, 1.3 percent higher at 310 pesos.
